quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO Matthew White): sales of $8.8 billion increased 6% over the prior year and 2% sequentially, including a 3% foreign-currency tailwind; excluding FX, underlying sales increased 3%, from 2% pricing and 1% volumes, with volume growth driven by project startups in the Americas and APAC while continued industrial softness in EMEA more than offset base volume growth in the Americas. Operating profit of $2.6 billion was up 4% at a 29.5% margin (full-year operating margin up 30 basis points); EPS of $4.20 increased 6%. He pointed to 17% growth in CapEx (period not specified on the call), 'led by spending for the record project backlog', and fourth-quarter share repurchases were stepped up to $1.4 billion. For full-year 2025, about $6 billion was invested for growth and $7.4 billion returned to owners; CEO Sanjiv Lamba said Linde achieved annual record EPS, operating cash flow and operating margins, with a 24.2% return on capital.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $8.8 billion (up 6%); operating profit $2.6 billion, 29.5% margin; EPS $4.20 (up 6%); CapEx growth 17%; 2025 return on capital 24.2%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance (CFO Matthew White): EPS projected in the range of $17.40 to $17.90, or 6% to 9% above 2025, assuming a 1% FX tailwind and 0% base volume change at the midpoint; the first-quarter outlook keeps the same baseline volume assumption with a 3% FX tailwind. Management called the guidance 'guarded, prudent, and I would say conservative', supported by the record project backlog, productivity, and additional restructuring actions initiated in the fourth quarter (predominantly headcount, the majority in the Engineering segment; bulk of the benefits expected in the second half of the year; cash paybacks on average about two years). CEO Sanjiv Lamba expects 2026 margin expansion to beat Linde's long-term range of 30 to 50 basis points per year.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 EPS $17.40 to $17.90 (6% to 9% above 2025); assumes 1% FX tailwind and 0% base volume change

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjiv Lamba: the project backlog stands at a record $10 billion, not including over half a billion dollars of investment for rocket propellants for contracted space launch customers; two-thirds of the backlog supports contracted clean energy projects. Linde 'remains the anchor industrial gas supplier for some of the largest and most successful clean energy and advanced electronics fabs in the world', and he is 'highly confident that we will announce new signature fab wins in the coming months'. Backlog trajectory: about a billion of projects started up in 2025; in 2026 (OCI Woodside start-up phased through the year) he expects $2.5 to $3 billion of projects to come off the backlog and start contributing to revenue, then to grow the backlog back, citing 'Some really large wins around fabs' in a fairly advanced pipeline. Asked whether the sale-of-gas backlog could return toward the analyst's $7 billion figure, he answered 'We will be heading towards that $7 billion mark'.
quarterly_data.figure: record project backlog $10 billion; $2.5 to $3 billion of projects to start up in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: End markets (CEO Sanjiv Lamba): the US remains a resilient market with sales up across almost every end market, where electronics and commercial space stand out for growth; across end markets 'electronics stands out, we are seeing good strong growth there', and he expects 'a lot more investment in that space', which he tied to the backlog. On US near-shoring efforts, which continue to progress, 'Semiconductors are well ahead', with other sectors also moving forward.

Advanced-node gas intensity (CEO Sanjiv Lamba, answering on TSMC's Phoenix fabs): after the yield from the first couple of fabs positively surprised, 'the commitment to major investments in advanced nodes at Phoenix is strong, and with that comes higher gas intensity'. Moving to advanced nodes raises gas usage per node and, 'more importantly', new gases are being introduced and used in much bigger quantities, which together raise overall gas intensity for the new fabs. 'The next round of fabs is now under discussion and being worked through.'

Helium and rare gases: CFO Matthew White said the two combined were about a one to 2% headwind on 2025 EPS, toward the upper end of that range, and that rare gas 'does feel a little bit better right now, especially with some of the electronics recovery'. CEO Sanjiv Lamba said helium pricing has been high single-digit negative for a few quarters, 'Helium is gonna be long in the medium term at least' (China long on Russian helium), and helium is a low single-digit business for Linde.
quarterly_data.figure: helium and rare gas about a one to 2% headwind on 2025 EPS (upper end of range)

connects_to.relationship: gas plants supplying TSMC's Arizona (Phoenix) Fab 1 and Fab 2

contracts.signal: Asked about TSMC's Arizona Fab 2, CEO Sanjiv Lamba said Linde's plants for Fab 1 and 2 are in operation ('those assets are on the ground. They have been commissioned'): Fab 1 is fully utilized, and Fab 2 is ramping up at TSMC's end 'and, obviously, we're there fully supporting them on that'. The next round of Phoenix fabs is under discussion, and advanced nodes bring higher gas intensity.
